SOURCE FACTS

What the records actually establish

  • GMU 578 boundaryWDFW geometry effective April 1, 2026–March 31, 2027. The published legal description controls if maps differ.
  • Quigley Butte (#3668)Historical WDFW PHS polygon: elk winter range. Reported precision one section; date not provided.
  • Trout Lake Marsh (#4664)Historical WDFW PHS: year-round elk concentration area. Original feature crosses GMU boundaries; only the GMU 578 intersection is displayed.
  • Husum–Conboy Lake (#5151)Historical WDFW PHS: varying elk concentrations and geographic shifts. Spring peaks in the source are not late-season bull counts.
  • 2025 GMU 578 general muzzleloader harvest13 bulls from 165 hunters; 8 five-points, 3 six-points or larger. Early and late seasons are combined; not a late-season probability.
  • Missing local movement dataNo GPS-derived 578 migration route was present in the archived mapped layer. No fabricated arrows or density probabilities are displayed.

Conboy Lake National Wildlife Refuge and Trout Lake Natural Area Preserve are not general elk-hunting access. Western Pacific Timber lands in Klickitat County have been closed to hunting access since September 1, 2023. Tract D and industrial gate rules require parcel-level checks.

GMU 578 independent field tool · No Atlas account, synchronization, or connection to the main Washington Hunt Atlas app. The GMU line and elk polygons are embedded and work without tiles. Street, topo, satellite and live forecasts need an internet connection. Optional WDFW land overlay shows WDFW-managed parcels only, not all ownership. Land ownership is not determined from a map tap; check posted boundaries before entry. Map location and pins are not transmitted to a server by this file.
